Remember this: librarians provide frontline services, library science teachers teach and research how to improve them, and data scientists use algorithms to process information. Their perspectives differ, but their foundations overlap.

It does not suit people seeking a low-pressure stable role, fearing research evaluations, or disliking teaching. University faculty do not follow simple office hours; publications and grants are invisible KPIs.

A common path is: earn a bachelor's degree in library and information science or information management, complete a required master's degree and usually a doctorate, enter academia as a lecturer, publish and win grants, earn promotion, then become a professor or academic leader.
This work suits people who love research, write academic papers, and enjoy sharing ideas in the classroom. If you can find interest in seemingly dry metadata, the field could fit you.

Postsecondary library science teachers teach courses in library science, information organization, digital libraries, and knowledge management; conduct research in library and information science; and supervise undergraduate and graduate study and theses. They connect information-science theory with library-sector practice.

paragraphs: A typical week includes classes from Monday through Friday, followed by grading and thesis supervision. Time between classes goes to literature research, writing papers, and revising grant applications. Evenings and weekends can bring conferences and online student discussions. Summer and winter breaks are often peak periods for completing projects and writing.

In short, they teach, conduct research, and supervise students. Work includes library and information science courses, thesis and project guidance, scholarship, program development, and professional support for libraries.

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show about 5,100 postsecondary library science teachers employed in 2024, projected to reach 5,300 by 2034. That is a net increase of about 200 jobs, with roughly 400 annual openings. Median annual pay is about $78,600 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace postsecondary library science teachers, but it will change course preparation and research. Literature research and organization once took days; AI now generates preliminary reviews, assists retrieval and classification, and produces course materials quickly. Yet teaching, scholarly judgment, and research supervision remain human responsibilities. AI provides drafts, while faculty decide whether they are correct, strong, and worth pursuing.

They teach library and information science courses, supervise theses and projects, conduct research, contribute to program development, and support library operations. In short: teach, research, and mentor students.
Librarians provide frontline reader services, while faculty teach and conduct research. One serves readers; the other develops information professionals and scholarship.

The burden comes from invisible evaluation: publications, grants, teaching, and student management all compete for time. Work has no fixed endpoint, and research continues through breaks, although schedules are relatively autonomous and students and scholarship provide meaning.
